Trump wants to talk about reducing nuclear arsenals at the trilateral talks on Thursday and is also set to bring up his war in Iran – but he is not expected to discuss Russia’s war in Ukraine, US officials said.

items.description:
Flights in the United States were resuming on Saturday after being grounded for several hours due to a major communications outage, though authorities said returning to normal operations would take time.
The nationwide stop sparked widespread chaos and left hundreds of thousands of passengers in limbo, with some pulled off planes moments before departure by airline staff who appeared in the dark about unfolding events.
Government officials said the incident was a major communications outage caused by decades old technology.

items.title: Wasim Akram questions Cummins’ Sandpapergate denial, says bowlers would spot tampering
items.description:
Pakistan pace legend Wasim Akram has questioned Australia captain Pat Cummins’ claim that he was unaware of the use of sandpaper during the 2018 ball-tampering scandal in South Africa, arguing that any experienced bowler would immediately recognise the difference between natural wear and deliberate damage to the ball.
Speaking in a video posted on social media on Saturday from Melbourne, Wasim said the marks left by sandpaper were distinctly different from those caused by normal contact with the ground.

items.description:
AI bots going rogue and humans using the technology for harm will likely be on the agenda when Donald Trump and Xi Jinping meet next week, with the Nvidia scandal hanging over the talks on AI safety.

items.description:

items.title: Yemeni govt forces fortify defences in Aden
items.description:

items.title: Fiscal surplus shrinks 40pc as revenues decline
items.description:
• Primary surplus drops to 2.1pc of GDP from 2.8pc last year  • Revenue falls despite higher tax collections; interest payments jump 23pc  • Provincial cash surpluses shrink 23pc; Balochistan posts deficit
ISLAMABAD: Pakistan’s fiscal buffers weakened in the first quarter of the current fiscal year despite expenditure controls and subsidy cuts, as revenue-to-GDP ratios declined and provincial cash surpluses shrank.
The overall fiscal surplus fell to 0.9 per cent of GDP in July-September this year from 1.7pc a year ago, according to fiscal operations data released by the Ministry of Finance.
